messages:
jen.k: Heads up: during a routine dev bucket audit I noticed some model snapshot artifacts contain full presigned S3 URLs inside debug metadata. The snapshots lived in `models/snapshots/dev/` and were briefly indexed by an internal search job. Potential exposure window ~2.5 hours.
sec-bot: Alert SEC-2026-143 created: unusual presigned URL pattern discovered in object metadata. Related GET spikes from 54.173.XX.XX observed 03:40-03:55 UTC.
infra_oncall: I'm pausing the indexing pipeline and scaling down `dev-search` and `model-sync` until we confirm. `kubectl scale deployment dev-search -n infra --replicas=0` and `kubectl scale deployment model-sync -n infra --replicas=0`
maria.s: Good. We need to rotate any credentials that could have generated those presigned URLs, and export access logs for `redwood-models-dev` for 00:00-06:00 UTC. Also block public read on that bucket immediately.
sam.t: I'll handle the IAM rotations. Rotating `model-sync` service account keys now and will update secrets. ETA 20m.
dev-ops: Bucket policy update going in: adding explicit Deny for principal '*' on s3:GetObject when aws:PrincipalType is Anonymous. Command: `aws s3api put-bucket-policy --bucket redwood-models-dev --policy file://deny-anon-get.json`
jen.k: Note: presigned URLs can't be revoked individually. Main mitigations are credential rotation + changing object permissions + preventing indexing. Also please snapshot and archive current object metadata for the postmortem.
product-security: Do we have any customers on the dev orgs? If so we need to prepare a customer-facing advisory. If not, prepare internal notification only.
maria.s: Initial grep across snapshots for `https://s3.amazonaws.com/.+X-Amz-Signature` pattern found 14 occurrences across 3 snapshots. No evidence yet of external request origins, but logs export requested. infra_oncall please include requester IPs, user agents, and request timestamps.
infra_oncall: Logs export in progress to s3://redwood-security-exports/SEC-2026-143/. Will also collect CloudTrail events for PutObject/GetObject on the bucket.
sam.t: Rotation done. model-sync service account keys rotated; updated in Secrets Manager and redeployed. Deployment shows 1/1 ready. I'll paste rotation steps into the SEC ticket.
sec-bot: Containment checklist: [1] pause indexing & sync jobs (done); [2] rotate service account credentials (done); [3] apply deny-anonymous bucket policy (in progress); [4] export access & cloudtrail logs (in progress); [5] search for other snapshots with presigned urls (in progress); [6] evaluate need to notify customers & compliance.
jen.k: Long-term action: we should stop embedding raw presigned URLs in snapshot metadata. Proposal: update model-sync to store object key references only and serve artifacts via gateway-signed short-lived tokens that check RBAC. QA this in staging, aim to canary in 2 weeks.
product-security: Also add requirement: MFA enforcement for any token/credential that can generate presigned URLs for models in dev and prod for the next 7 days while we audit.
maria.s: I'll temporarily disable model publish for dev orgs and enforce MFA on new publish tokens for 72 hours.
dev-ops: Quick grep shows no GETs from known customer IP ranges in the window so far. Still waiting on full CloudTrail.
jen.k: Thanks all. I'll open the postmortem draft in the SEC board and tag infra/dev leads. Please add any commands you ran and timelines.
sec-bot: Incident status: containment. Next update in 30 minutes or earlier if Logs show external access. Assigned: sam.t -> rotation notes & runbook update; infra_oncall -> logs export & bucket policy; maria.s -> publish lock & MFA policy; jen.k -> scan & postmortem.
product-security: If logs show external access, we need to escalate to legal/compliance. For now treat as internal exposure but proceed as if customer impact possible.
jen.k: Will do. Posting summary to #security-updates after log review. :lock:
